docs.title: AI Code Review for GitLab
docs.text:
Inline AI code review on every GitLab merge request, using your own model and your own keys.

ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin is a small open-source CLI that reads a merge request diff, asks an LLM to review each hunk, and posts the feedback as inline discussion threads on the exact lines that changed.

  • Inline comments, on the changed line, not one giant wall of text
  • Bring your own model: Claude on AWS Bedrock, the Anthropic API, Gemini, or any OpenAI-compatible / Ollama endpoint
  • Your code stays in your cloud: runs inside your own GitLab runners and calls only the provider you configure
  • Zero-flag setup in GitLab CI: picks up CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID, CI_MERGE_REQUEST_PROJECT_ID and CI_API_V4_URL automatically
  • Custom prompts from a local file or S3, so you can enforce your team's own review checklist
  • Quiet when there's nothing to say: hunks without significant feedback are rolled into a single summary note
  • MIT licensed and free: you only pay your LLM provider

docs.title: Quick start (60 seconds)
docs.text:
1. Create a project or group access token with the api scope and add it as a masked CI/CD variable called CODE_REVIEW_GITLAB_TOKEN.
  2. Add your provider key as a masked CI/CD variable, for example GEMINI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
  3. Add this job to .gitlab-ci.yml:
ai-code-review:
  image: node:20
  variables:
    AI_PROVIDER: gemini        # or: anthropic | bedrock | openai
  script:
    - npx -y @parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

Open a merge request. Review comments appear on the diff within a minute or two.

Prefer a one-line include?

Use the reusable CI template or the prebuilt Docker image to skip the npm install on every pipeline.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
MR pipeline ──► fetch every MR diff (GitLab API, all pages)
             ──► skip lockfiles, generated code and files unchanged since the last review
             ──► send each file's diff (+ the full file and MR description) to your LLM
             ──► LLM answers with JSON: line, severity, comment, optional fix
             ──► post each finding inline on the exact line, with a one-click suggestion
             ──► create or update one summary note on the MR

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Pick a provider and its recommended model
  • Customise the review prompt for your team's standards
  • See how it compares to GitLab Duo, CodeRabbit and PR-Agent

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Exact-line comments with severity. The model now answers in JSON (line, severity, comment, optional fix), so each comment is placed on the line it is about instead of the end of the hunk. Fixes are posted as one-click GitLab suggestion blocks.
  • No duplicate comments on new pushes. The summary note records the last reviewed commit. A rerun on the same commit does nothing, a new push reviews only the files that changed, and a line that already has a comment from the tool is not commented on again. The summary note is updated in place.
  • Better context. Each file is reviewed as a whole (all its hunks in one request), together with the full file content when it is small enough (--file-context-chars) and the MR title and description.
  • Noise controls: --include / --exclude globs with built-in excludes for lockfiles, vendored, minified and generated files; --min-severity; --max-files; --max-file-diff-lines.
  • --fail-on <severity> to fail the job (and block merges) on serious findings.
  • --dry-run prints the comments and the summary instead of posting them.
  • .ai-review.yml repository config file (--config).
  • --concurrency (default 2) to review files in parallel, and --timeout for AI requests.
  • Token usage (including cached tokens) is logged at the end of each run.
  • Anthropic: the system prompt is cached across files (prompt caching), and server-side refusal fallbacks are enabled on models that support them.
  • CI template inputs min_severity and fail_on.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• New default prompts focused on bugs, security and real performance problems: no praise sections, no style nitpicks, no blanket "add unit tests".
  • The Anthropic provider uses the official @anthropic-ai/sdk.
  • A custom prompt that cannot be loaded now fails the job instead of silently using the default prompt.
  • The job exits with code 1 when any file could not be reviewed or a comment could not be posted. The summary note lists what failed.
  • The CI template's default image is pinned to the release instead of latest.
  • typescript and @types/* moved to devDependencies, so npx installs less.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• MRs with more than 20 files were only partly reviewed: the /diffs endpoint is paginated and only the first page was read.
  • Bedrock requests failed on current Claude models, which reject temperature and top_p. Sampling parameters are no longer sent to any provider.
  • The Gemini API key could leak into CI logs: it was sent in the URL and failed requests were logged in full. It is now sent in the x-goog-api-key header, and errors are logged without URLs or headers. The fake browser User-Agent was removed.
  • Rate limits could loop forever and re-bill the model: retries are now bounded (4 attempts, exponential backoff, Retry-After honoured), cover 5xx and network errors, work for every provider, and never repeat the model call when only posting to GitLab failed.
  • Hunk headers without a line count (@@ -5 +5 @@) put comments one line off.
  • \ No newline at end of file was treated as a code line and could make GitLab reject the comment.
  • Files that were renamed and modified were not reviewed.
  • Comments that GitLab rejects because of their position are posted as a general MR comment instead of being lost.
  • No timeouts on HTTP requests: a stuck provider could hang the job until the CI timeout.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Zero-flag GitLab CI setup: project ID, MR IID and API URL are read from CI_MERGE_REQUEST_PROJECT_ID, CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID and CI_API_V4_URL. Every flag also has an environment-variable fallback (see the docs).
  • Anthropic API provider (--ai-provider anthropic).
  • OpenAI-compatible provider (--ai-provider openai) for OpenAI, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, LiteLLM and OpenRouter.
  • --api-url option to point any provider at a custom base URL.
  • Reusable GitLab CI template with inputs (templates/ai-code-review.yml), usable with a single include: remote.
  • Docker image published to ghcr.io/parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin.
  • Small "Reviewed by" footer on the summary note. Disable it with --no-attribution or AI_REVIEW_ATTRIBUTION=false.
  • Documentation site, test suite and CI.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Default Gemini model is now gemini-3.5-flash (gemini-1.5-flash has been retired).
  • Default Bedrock model is now the us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 inference profile.
  • Explicit --custom-model / --region now take precedence over AWS_BEDROCK_MODEL / AWS_REGION.
  • Node.js 20+ is required.
  • Missing configuration is reported all at once, with a clear message.
  • GitLab connection failures now fail the job instead of continuing silently.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• package.json main and description (npm listing).
  • Summary note line numbers no longer print undefined.
  • Review errors other than 429 are now logged instead of swallowed.

docs.title: 0.0.11 and earlier
docs.text: See the GitHub releases.

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text:
There are several good ways to get AI review on GitLab merge requests. Here's an honest look at where this project fits.

ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin GitLab Duo Code Review CodeRabbit PR-Agent (Qodo, open source) License / cost MIT, free (you pay your LLM) Paid GitLab add-on SaaS, paid plans Open source (AGPL) Runs where Your GitLab runners GitLab Vendor cloud Self-hosted or vendor Bring your own model Bedrock, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI-compatible, Ollama Limited No Yes (many providers) Setup One CI job / one include Enable the add-on Install app Webhook server or CI job Inline line comments ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Custom prompts from S3 / repo ✅ – Config-based Config-based Footprint <2,000 lines of TypeScript, single CLI – – Large Python project with many tools

docs.title: When to choose this project
docs.text:
• You want something small and auditable that your security team can read in one sitting.
  • You're on AWS and want reviews to go through Bedrock in your own account.
  • You want a CI-native job with no extra server, webhook service or SaaS app.
  • You need air-gapped reviews with a local model via Ollama.

docs.title: When to choose something else
docs.text:
• You want chat-style interaction on the MR (/ask, /improve commands), auto-generated descriptions and many other tools: look at PR-Agent or CodeRabbit.
  • You're already paying for GitLab Duo and want a first-party, zero-setup experience: use Duo Code Review.

Feature details for other products change often. Check their own documentation for the current state, and open an issue if something here is out of date.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Thanks for helping out! Issues, ideas and pull requests are all welcome.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin.git
cd ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin
npm ci
npm test          # builds with tsc, then runs node:test suites in test/

docs.title: Adding a provider
docs.text:
1. Implement AICodeReviewClient (complete({system, user})) in src/<provider>.ts. Throw the provider's original error, with its HTTP status, so withRetry() in src/retry.ts can retry 429s and 5xx. Never log request URLs or headers.
  2. Add it to PROVIDERS and the env-var mapping in src/config.ts.
  3. Wire it in createAIClient() in src/index.ts.
  4. Add a test in test/providers.test.js (there's a tiny fake HTTP server helper) and a page under docs/providers/.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
mkdocs serve      # http://127.0.0.1:8000

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
• Keep PRs focused. Add or update tests and docs alongside code.
  • npm test and mkdocs build --strict must pass (CI checks both).
  • Add a line to CHANGELOG.md.

docs.text: Look for the good first issue label.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Does my code leave my infrastructure? Only the diff hunks are sent, and only to the provider you configure. With Bedrock they stay in your AWS account. With Ollama they never leave your network.

How much does it cost? The tool is free. You pay your LLM provider per token. Each hunk is one request containing the hunk plus the prompts (around 1k tokens of prompt).

Does it review the whole file or only the diff? Only the changed hunks, which keeps reviews focused and cheap.

Can I use it on GitHub? No. It's built for GitLab merge requests.

Can I stop it commenting on trivial things? Yes. Raise --min-severity to major (or critical) to post only important findings, and tighten the custom prompt.

Will it comment again on every push? No. The tool remembers the last reviewed commit in its summary note, reviews only files changed since then, and never posts a second comment on a line it has already commented on.

Can it block merges? Yes. Set --fail-on major (or AI_REVIEW_FAIL_ON) and allow_failure: false on the job.

Can I remove the "Reviewed by" footer? Yes. Use --no-attribution or AI_REVIEW_ATTRIBUTION=false. It only appears on the summary note.

docs.title: "Missing required configuration"
docs.text: The CLI lists every missing setting. In CI, make sure the job runs in a merge request pipeline (rules: - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"), otherwise CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID is not set.

docs.title: "Failed to load merge request from GitLab: 401/403/404"
docs.text:
• The token needs the api scope and at least Developer access on the project.
  • Masked protected variables are not available on unprotected branches.
  • On self-managed GitLab, check --gitlab-api-url ends in /api/v4.

docs.title: No comments appear
docs.text:
• The model may have found nothing significant. The AI code review summary note lists the files with no comments.
  • Files may have been skipped. The summary note lists files that were excluded by path filters, too large (--max-file-diff-lines) or over the file limit (--max-files).
  • Findings below --min-severity are not posted.
  • The commit may already have been reviewed: the tool reviews each commit once and only re-reviews files that changed. Use --no-incremental to review everything again.
  • Deleted files, pure renames and binary files are skipped.
  • Check the job log for Failed to review <file> lines. Run with --dry-run locally to see what the model returns.

docs.title: The job fails after posting comments
docs.text: The job exits with code 1 when a file could not be reviewed or a comment could not be posted (see the summary note), or when --fail-on is set and a finding reaches that severity. The reusable CI template uses allow_failure: true by default, so this never blocks a merge unless you change it.

docs.title: AWS Bedrock
docs.text:
• "The provided model identifier is invalid" / "on-demand throughput isn't supported": use an inference profile ID (us.anthropic.…). See Bedrock.
  • AccessDeniedException: enable model access in the Bedrock console and check the IAM policy.
  • Throttling: requests are retried with backoff (see below). For large MRs, request a quota increase, lower --concurrency or use a smaller model.

docs.title: Gemini
docs.text:
• 404 model not found: older models (for example gemini-1.5-*) have been retired. Set GEMINI_MODEL to a current stable model.
  • 400 API key not valid: create a new key in Google AI Studio.

docs.title: Rate limits (any provider)
docs.text: Rate limits (429), server errors (5xx) and network errors are retried up to 4 times with exponential backoff, honouring Retry-After. If a file still fails, it is listed in the summary note, the job exits with code 1, and the file is reviewed again on the next run. Lower --concurrency (default 2) if you hit rate limits often.

docs.title: Repository config file
docs.text:
Put an .ai-review.yml file at the root of the repository to configure the review for that project without touching CI variables. It is read from $CI_PROJECT_DIR (the checkout of the merge request's source branch), or from the path given with --config / AI_REVIEW_CONFIG.

Precedence: CLI flag → environment variable → .ai-review.yml → default.

# .ai-review.yml
include:            # only review these paths (default: everything)
  - src/**
  - lib/**
exclude:            # skip these paths, on top of the built-in excludes
  - "**/*.test.ts"
  - migrations/**
default_excludes: true     # skip lockfiles, vendored, minified and generated files
min_severity: major        # post only major and critical findings
fail_on: critical          # exit 1 if any critical finding is found (default: none)
max_files: 50              # review at most 50 files per run (0 = no limit)
max_file_diff_lines: 1500  # skip files with more changed lines than this
file_context_chars: 30000  # send the full file as context when it is this small (0 = never)
concurrency: 2             # files reviewed in parallel
incremental: true          # only review files changed since the last reviewed commit
system_prompt_path: .gitlab/ai-review/system_prompt.txt
code_review_prompt_path: .gitlab/ai-review/code_review_prompt.txt

docs.title: Globs
docs.text:
Patterns work like .gitignore:

  • A pattern without / matches the file name in any directory: *.lock, package-lock.json.
  • * matches within one directory, ** matches any number of directories: src/**/*.ts.
  • exclude wins over include.

The built-in excludes are: package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lockb, *.lock, go.sum, *.min.js, *.min.css, *.map, *.snap, *.svg, *.pb.go, *_pb2.py, *.generated.*, **/vendor/**, **/node_modules/**, **/dist/**. Turn them off with default_excludes: false.

Note

The file comes from the merge request's own branch, so an author can change it in their merge request. Use CI/CD variables for settings that must be enforced, such as AI_REVIEW_FAIL_ON.

docs.title: Custom prompts
docs.text:
Two prompts drive every review:

  • System prompt: the reviewer's persona and what to look for (default)
  • Code review prompt: how to review each file and how to rate severity (default)

Override either with a local path (for example a file committed to the repository under review) or an s3://bucket/key URL shared across many projects.

ai-code-review:
  variables:
    SYSTEM_PROMPT_PATH: .gitlab/ai-review/system_prompt.txt
    CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PATH: s3://my-org-prompts/code_review_prompt.txt
    S3_REGION: eu-west-1

The paths can also go in the repository config file.

If a custom prompt can't be loaded, the job fails with an error. It does not silently fall back to the built-in prompt, so a broken checklist never goes unnoticed.

docs.title: The output format is added for you
docs.text:
The tool always appends its own output instructions to your prompts: the model must answer with JSON listing a line, a severity (critical, major, minor) and a comment for each finding, with an optional replacement for the line. That is what lets the tool place comments on the exact line, offer one-click GitLab suggestions, and filter by severity.

So your prompts only need to say what to review. You don't need to describe the response format, and older prompts that say "reply with 204" keep working: a 204 answer is treated as "no comments".

docs.title: Example: team-specific checklist
docs.text:
You are a senior engineer reviewing a Go microservice.
Focus only on: correctness, error handling, context propagation,
SQL injection, missing tests for new exported functions.
Ignore formatting and naming. Keep each comment under 50 words.
Rate anything that can lose data or leak credentials as critical.

docs.text:
AI_REVIEW_CONFIG, AI_REVIEW_INCLUDE, AI_REVIEW_EXCLUDE, AI_REVIEW_DEFAULT_EXCLUDES, AI_REVIEW_MIN_SEVERITY, AI_REVIEW_FAIL_ON, AI_REVIEW_MAX_FILES, AI_REVIEW_MAX_FILE_DIFF_LINES, AI_REVIEW_FILE_CONTEXT_CHARS, AI_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY, AI_REVIEW_TIMEOUT, AI_REVIEW_DRY_RUN, AI_REVIEW_INCREMENTAL. See CLI options for what each one does.

CI_PROJECT_DIR (set by GitLab) is where .ai-review.yml is looked up.

docs.title: CLI options
docs.text:
Precedence: CLI flag → environment variable → config file → default.

Option Env fallback Default Description -g, --gitlab-api-url CI_API_V4_URL https://gitlab.com/api/v4 GitLab API base URL -t, --gitlab-access-token CODE_REVIEW_GITLAB_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN – Token with api scope (required) -p, --project-id CI_MERGE_REQUEST_PROJECT_ID, CI_PROJECT_ID – Project ID (required) -m, --merge-request-id CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID – Merge request IID (required) -a, --ai-provider AI_PROVIDER gemini gemini, bedrock, anthropic, openai -k, --api-key provider-specific, see env vars – API key / AWS access key ID -s, --api-secret AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY – AWS secret key (Bedrock only) -u, --api-url AI_API_URL + provider-specific provider default Base URL of the AI API -r, --region AWS_REGION us-east-1 AWS region (Bedrock) -c, --custom-model AI_MODEL + provider-specific provider default Model ID -sp, --system-prompt-path SYSTEM_PROMPT_PATH built-in Local path or s3://bucket/key -crp, --code-review-prompt-path CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT_PATH built-in Local path or s3://bucket/key --s3-region S3_REGION AWS_REGION Region for S3 prompt files --s3-access-key S3_ACCESS_KEY – Credentials for S3 prompt files --s3-secret-key S3_SECRET_KEY – Credentials for S3 prompt files --no-attribution AI_REVIEW_ATTRIBUTION=false attribution on Remove the small "Reviewed by" footer from the summary note

docs.title: Review behaviour
docs.text:
These can also be set in .ai-review.yml.

Option Env fallback Default Description --config AI_REVIEW_CONFIG .ai-review.yml if present Repository config file --include AI_REVIEW_INCLUDE everything Comma-separated globs; only matching files are reviewed --exclude AI_REVIEW_EXCLUDE – Comma-separated globs to skip, on top of the built-in excludes --no-default-excludes AI_REVIEW_DEFAULT_EXCLUDES=false excludes on Also review lockfiles, vendored, minified and generated files --min-severity AI_REVIEW_MIN_SEVERITY minor Lowest severity to post: minor, major, critical --fail-on AI_REVIEW_FAIL_ON none Exit with code 1 when a finding is at or above this severity --max-files AI_REVIEW_MAX_FILES 50 Review at most this many files per run (0 = no limit) --max-file-diff-lines AI_REVIEW_MAX_FILE_DIFF_LINES 1500 Skip files with more changed lines than this --file-context-chars AI_REVIEW_FILE_CONTEXT_CHARS 30000 Send the full file as context when it is at most this many characters (0 = never) --concurrency AI_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY 2 Files reviewed in parallel --timeout AI_REVIEW_TIMEOUT 120 Seconds before an AI request times out --dry-run AI_REVIEW_DRY_RUN=true off Print comments and the summary instead of posting them --no-incremental AI_REVIEW_INCREMENTAL=false incremental on Review every file on every run

docs.title: How repeat runs behave
docs.text:
The summary note records the last fully reviewed commit. On the next pipeline the tool:

  1. Does nothing if that commit is the current head (for example, a retried job).
  2. Otherwise reviews only files changed since that commit. After a force push it reviews every file.
  3. Never posts a second comment on a line that already has one from the tool.
  4. Updates the same summary note instead of adding a new one.

If any file fails to review, the checkpoint is not moved forward, so the next run tries again.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Review finished 1 Invalid configuration, GitLab unreachable, a file could not be reviewed or a comment could not be posted, or a finding reached --fail-on

If required settings are missing, the CLI lists all of them at once and exits with code 1.

docs.title: Reusable CI template (one-line include)
docs.text:
The repository ships a reusable GitLab CI template with inputs, templates/ai-code-review.yml. Include it straight from GitHub and pin a release tag:

include:
  - remote: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin/0.1.0/templates/ai-code-review.yml
    inputs:
      provider: anthropic

This adds an ai-code-review job that runs in merge request pipelines and uses the prebuilt Docker image. Credentials still come from your CI/CD variables (see GitLab CI setup).

Pin a tag

Always include a release tag (for example 0.1.0), not main, so the job only changes when you choose to upgrade.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Default Description stage test Stage the job runs in provider gemini gemini, bedrock, anthropic or openai model (provider default) Model ID override image ghcr.io/parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin:<release> Image that contains the CLI, pinned to the same release as the template allow_failure true Don't block the pipeline if the review fails min_severity minor Lowest severity posted as a comment: minor, major, critical fail_on none Fail the job on a finding at or above this severity when on_success on_success (every MR pipeline) or manual

docs.title: Overriding the job
docs.text:
Anything not covered by inputs can be overridden by redefining keys on the ai-code-review job after the include:

ai-code-review:
  tags: [docker]
  variables:
    SYSTEM_PROMPT_PATH: .gitlab/ai-review/system_prompt.txt

docs.title: Runners without internet access
docs.text: If your runners can't reach raw.githubusercontent.com, copy templates/ai-code-review.yml into your repository and use include: local with the same inputs.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
npm i -g @parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin

Requires Node.js 20 or newer.

export CODE_REVIEW_GITLAB_TOKEN=glpat-...
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...

ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin \
  --gitlab-api-url https://gitlab.com/api/v4 \
  --project-id 123 \
  --merge-request-id 45 \
  --ai-provider anthropic

Every flag can also be supplied as an environment variable. See CLI options and environment variables.

docs.title: Docker image
docs.text:
A prebuilt image is published to GitHub Container Registry on every release:

ghcr.io/parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin:latest
ghcr.io/parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin:<version>

It is multi-arch (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) and has no ENTRYPOINT, so it works directly as a GitLab CI job image:

ai-code-review:
  image: ghcr.io/parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin:latest
  variables:
    AI_PROVIDER: bedrock
  script:
    - ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

docs.title: Running locally
docs.text:
docker run --rm \
  -e CODE_REVIEW_GITLAB_TOKEN -e GEMINI_API_KEY \
  ghcr.io/parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin:latest \
  ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin --project-id 123 --merge-request-id 45

docs.title: GitLab CI (npm)
docs.text: The simplest setup: run the CLI from npm in any Node 20+ image.

docs.title: 1. Create a GitLab token
docs.text:
The tool posts discussions on merge requests, so it needs a token with the api scope. A project access token with the Developer role is recommended. The comments then appear under a bot user rather than your personal account.

Add it under Settings → CI/CD → Variables as CODE_REVIEW_GITLAB_TOKEN (masked, and protected if you only review protected branches).

docs.title: 2. Add provider credentials
docs.text: Provider CI/CD variables Gemini GEMINI_API_KEY Anthropic API ANTHROPIC_API_KEY AWS Bedrock AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION OpenAI-compatible OPENAI_API_KEY (optional for Ollama), OPENAI_BASE_URL, AI_MODEL

docs.title: 3. Add the job
docs.text:
ai-code-review:
  stage: test
  image: node:20
  variables:
    AI_PROVIDER: anthropic
  script:
    - npx -y @parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
  allow_failure: true

Why merge_request_event?

CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID and CI_MERGE_REQUEST_PROJECT_ID are only set in merge request pipelines. In a branch pipeline you must pass --project-id and --merge-request-id explicitly.

docs.title: Run only on demand
docs.text:
Change the rule to when: manual to add a ▶ button on the MR pipeline instead of reviewing every push:

  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
      when: manual

docs.title: Pin a version
docs.text: npx -y @parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin@0.1.0 keeps upgrades under your control.

docs.title: Self-managed GitLab
docs.text:
Everything works on self-managed GitLab:

  • In CI, the API URL is taken from CI_API_V4_URL, so no configuration is needed.
  • Outside CI, pass --gitlab-api-url https://gitlab.your-company.com/api/v4.
  • The reusable CI template works on self-managed GitLab too. If runners can't reach GitHub, copy it in and use include: local.
  • For air-gapped environments, pair it with Ollama or another self-hosted model and the Docker image mirrored into your registry.

docs.title: Trigger via the GitLab API
docs.text:
Create a new merge request pipeline, which runs the review job:

curl --request POST \
  --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: $GITLAB_TOKEN" \
  "https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/$PROJECT_ID/merge_requests/$MR_IID/pipelines"

You can call this from chat-ops bots, scheduled jobs, or other automation.

docs.title: Trigger on reviewer assignment (webhook)
docs.text:
Run the review only when a specific user (for example a bot account) is added as a reviewer.

  1. In your GitLab project go to Settings → Webhooks and add a webhook:
    • URL: your handler endpoint (for example an AWS Lambda function URL)
    • Trigger: Merge request events
    • Secret token: a random string your handler verifies
  2. Configure the review job with when: manual or a variable-gated rule, so that it only runs when the handler triggers it.
  3. Deploy a handler like this one:
exports.handler = async (event) => {
  if (event.headers['x-gitlab-token'] !== process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET) {
    return { statusCode: 401 };
  }
  const payload = JSON.parse(event.body);
  if (payload.object_kind !== 'merge_request') return { statusCode: 200 };

  const botUserId = Number(process.env.REVIEW_BOT_USER_ID);
  const reviewers = payload.changes?.reviewers?.current || [];
  if (!reviewers.some((r) => r.id === botUserId)) return { statusCode: 200 };

  // Start a new merge request pipeline
  await fetch(
    `https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/${payload.project.id}` +
    `/merge_requests/${payload.object_attributes.iid}/pipelines`,
    { method: 'POST', headers: { 'PRIVATE-TOKEN': process.env.GITLAB_TOKEN } },
  );
  return { statusCode: 200 };
};

docs.title: Anthropic API
docs.text:
Call Claude directly with an Anthropic API key. No cloud account is needed.

Variable Flag Notes AI_PROVIDER=anthropic -a anthropic ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -k ANTHROPIC_MODEL or AI_MODEL -c Default claude-sonnet-5-5 ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or AI_API_URL -u Optional, for proxies or gateways

See Anthropic's models overview for current model IDs. A faster, cheaper model (for example a Haiku-class model) works well for large merge requests.

ai-code-review:
  image: node:20
  variables:
    AI_PROVIDER: anthropic
  script:
    - npx -y @parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

docs.title: AWS Bedrock (Claude)
docs.text: Bedrock keeps every request inside your AWS account and region, which is often the easiest provider to get approved by security teams.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Variable Flag Notes AI_PROVIDER=bedrock -a bedrock AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID -k AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY -s AWS_REGION -r Default us-east-1 AWS_BEDROCK_MODEL or AI_MODEL -c Default us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

docs.title: Choosing a model ID
docs.text:
Newer Claude models on Bedrock must be invoked through a cross-region inference profile. That is the model ID with a geography prefix such as us., eu., apac. or global., not the bare anthropic.… ID. To list the profiles available to your account:

aws bedrock list-inference-profiles --region us-east-1 \
  --query "inferenceProfileSummaries[?contains(inferenceProfileId, 'claude')].inferenceProfileId"

Make sure model access is enabled for that model in the Bedrock console.

docs.title: IAM permissions
docs.text:
The access key needs bedrock:InvokeModel on the inference profile and on the underlying foundation models it routes to:

{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": "bedrock:InvokeModel",
  "Resource": [
    "arn:aws:bedrock:*:*:inference-profile/*",
    "arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.*"
  ]
}

docs.title: Example job
docs.text:
ai-code-review:
  image: node:20
  variables:
    AI_PROVIDER: bedrock
    AWS_REGION: us-east-1
  script:
    - npx -y @parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

docs.title: Google Gemini
docs.text:
Variable Flag Notes AI_PROVIDER=gemini -a gemini Default provider GEMINI_API_KEY -k Create one in Google AI Studio GEMINI_MODEL or AI_MODEL -c Default gemini-3.5-flash GEMINI_API_URL or AI_API_URL -u Default https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com

Use a stable model name without a -preview or -latest suffix in CI, so reviews don't change behaviour unexpectedly. The current list is on Google's Gemini models page.

docs.title: OpenAI-compatible endpoints & Ollama
docs.text:
The openai provider talks to any server that implements the OpenAI Chat Completions API (POST /chat/completions). That covers OpenAI itself plus self-hosted and gateway options.

Variable Flag Notes AI_PROVIDER=openai -a openai OPENAI_BASE_URL or AI_API_URL -u Default https://api.openai.com/v1 OPENAI_API_KEY -k Optional; omitted for servers that don't need auth OPENAI_MODEL or AI_MODEL -c Required

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Ollama (fully local)OpenAILiteLLM / OpenRouter / vLLM 
ai-code-review:
  image: node:20
  variables:
    AI_PROVIDER: openai
    OPENAI_BASE_URL: http://ollama.internal:11434/v1
    AI_MODEL: qwen2.5-coder:14b
  script:
    - npx -y @parvez3019/ai-code-review-gitlab-plugin
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

No code ever leaves your network. The runner just needs to reach the Ollama host.

variables:
  AI_PROVIDER: openai
  AI_MODEL: <model id>
  # OPENAI_API_KEY set as a masked CI/CD variable

variables:
  AI_PROVIDER: openai
  OPENAI_BASE_URL: https://your-gateway.example.com/v1
  AI_MODEL: <model id as exposed by the gateway>

Tip

Smaller local models follow the JSON output format less reliably. When an answer isn't valid JSON, it is posted as one comment on the last changed line of the file. If you get noisy reviews, try a larger model, raise --min-severity, or tighten the prompt.
